content: PanoRef coverage-engine implementation review: algorithm architecture rated 8/10, search-mode correctness 7.5/10, readiness for complex imported sets 4/10; overall promising but not production-ready. Strengths include deterministic surface sampling proportional to world-space area via barycentric coordinates, origin evaluation covering occlusion, geometric face normals, viewing angle, projected texel density, separate visibility/usable-coverage bitsets, and continuous quality values, plus a genuinely joint pair mode that checks every legal coarse pair, ranks by bitset union, then applies quality/contribution tie-breakers, and a shared coarse-to-fine engine (4,096 coarse samples, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine samples, local offsets, separate fixed-first/joint branches). Tests cover deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, and both search modes. Key blocker: imported sets can produce zero legal candidates because non-floor objects store their entire AABB as an obstacle, clearance is distance from origin to AABB, and points inside an AABB get zero distance and are rejected; this affects single-GLB Maya sets, combined room shell/furniture meshes, concave geometry, L-shaped walls, and large models whose AABB contains empty navigable space. Proposed fix: use actual geometry clearance (camera sphere/capsule does not intersect nearby triangles) via coverage BVH point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast, and make obstacle bounds per connected mesh or spatial cluster rather than per imported set object, plus add a regression test. Next actions: rebase onto main and resolve PR conflict; add allowed-floor-region mechanism or robust imported-floor component filtering; run one real complex imported-set benchmark and add a full 100K+ optimizer integration test (not just BVH construction); then spawn a subagent to disprove completion, fix remaining holes, and repeat until no holes are found. Implementation artifacts include projected style materials with uniforms for secondary pano map, secondary origin, yaw, occlusion cube, near/far, face size, debug coverage, primary/secondary texel constants, and a projectedQualityAt function computing offset, distance squared, direction, geometric normal via cross(dFdy, dFdx), facing = abs(dot(normal, -direction)), angleQuality = smoothstep(0.15, 0.55, facing), texelDensity = texelConstant * facing / distanceSquared, resolutionQuality = smoothstep(128, 1024, texelDensity), returning angleQuality * resolutionQuality. Test results: multiOriginInteraction.test.ts 36/36 passed; full unit run 371 tests including both optimizer modes over 101,250 triangles, TypeScript, production build, and WebGL compile/pixel checks all passed; 22 desktop/mobile Playwright scenarios passed including optimizer completion and overlapping-drawer regression; goal:smoke build→reference→shots→export produced a valid 33.1 MB package. Git diff shows 16 files changed (307 insertions, 216 deletions) including surfaceSampler.ts (+125), projectionCoverage.test.ts (+59), multiOriginInteraction.test.ts (+8), projectorOcclusion.test.ts (+20), and origin/main is an ancestor of HEAD.

Audit round three found two stale-state holes: editing bounds after a completed run leaves the old result and origin-apply actions visible, even if those origins are outside the newly displayed region; changing the primary panorama does not refresh the untouched default region or invalidate a fixed-first result; the region remains centered on the previous panorama. The in-flight locking fix itself works. PR publication, ancestry, benchmark evidence, heavy integration test, worker/refinement constraints, docs, and verification remain sound. Round three fix: centralize result invalidation for every optimizer input and synchronize only untouched default bounds to the active capture origin, preserving user-authored bounds.

CoverageOptimizerPanel implementation reached production-ready status after iterative adversarial auditing. The engine uses deterministic surface sampling proportional to world-space area via barycentric coordinates, double-sided BVH occlusion queries, and two search modes (fixed-first and joint-pair) sharing a coarse-to-fine pipeline (4,096 coarse, 256 candidates, 24,576 fine samples). Initial blockers included imported-set clearance failures (AABB-based distance rejecting interior points) and large-prop tabletop acceptance; fixes added geometry-accurate clearance via BVH point-to-triangle distance, per-mesh obstacle bounds, allowed-floor-region constraints, and regression tests. The UI component (React with useState/useRef, async analyze with cancellation/AbortError handling, search-mode Select) underwent four audit rounds finding: (1) editable bounds during running analysis not canceling in-flight jobs → disabled controls during running state; (2) stale results after completed runs when bounds edited post-completion or panorama changed → centralized result invalidation and synchronized default bounds; (3) stale extraction failures bypassing analysis-identity check → added identity guard to extraction catch. Final state: PR #23 MERGEABLE/CLEAN, local/remote heads match at c1f6c8d rebased on origin/main, 373/373 tests pass including 101,250-triangle two-mode optimizer, WebGL compile/pixel checks, 22 Playwright scenarios, 33.1 MB workflow export, real production benchmark with no page errors. Independent auditor confirmed no remaining concrete holes after six rounds. Documentation corrected from 303→373 test count.
